newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mayors seek funds for housing programs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mayors seek funds for housing programs.

text.p: U.S. mayors adopted resolutions on Tuesday urging President Clinton and Congress to support existing low-income housing programs and expand policies to aid economically-distressed communities.
The U.S. Conference of Mayors, meeting in San Francisco, approved resolutions urging:

* Congress to maintain, and the Clinton administration to support, the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, the largest federal program to fund the development and rehabilitation of housing for low-income households.
* President Clinton and Congress to enact bi-partisan legislation to authorize an expansion of the Empowerment Zone and Enterprise Community program.
* President Clinton and Congress to refrain from cuts to Community Development Block Grant levels in fiscal year 1998, and to end the on-going proliferation of set-asides.
* President Clinton and Congress to preserve the existing supply of multifamily rental housing and units and project-based subsidies for the very low-income population.
